docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Infinity Extraction is a comprehensive document processing system tailored for enterprise-level applications. It enables advanced text extraction, table detection, visual question answering (VQA), and large language model (LLM) evaluation, with a focus on scalability and observability. These elements can be utilised in creating an end to end document extraction application.

Leveraging state-of-the-art models like YOLOv10, Microsoft's Table Transformer (TATR), and PaddleNLP, it handles various document types, including PDFs and images, to extract structured and unstructured data efficiently. The system includes robust preprocessing tools, layout detection, data extraction, LLM evaluation metrics, and OpenTelemetry-based observability, making it ideal for complex document workflows.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: Infinity Extraction is a powerful document processing system designed for enterprise-level applications, enabling text extraction, table detection, visual question answering, and more with scalability and observability. Below are the steps to get started.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.10: Required for compatibility with the library.
  • System Requirements: Linux-based system (e.g., Ubuntu) with internet access for dependency installation.
  • Docker: Required for setting up the observability dashboard.
  • Git: For cloning the repository.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
1. Install Python 3.10: Install Python 3.10 using the following commands in bash terminal:

sudo apt update
sudo apt upgrade
sudo apt autoremove
sudo add-apt-repository ppa:deadsnakes/ppa
sudo apt update
sudo apt install python3.10 python3.10-venv python3.10-distutils python3.10-dev -y

curl -sS https://bootstrap.pypa.io/get-pip.py | sudo python3.10
2. Install Docker: Install docker in the system using the following bash commands for observability: 

sudo apt update
sudo apt install \
ca-certificates \
curl \
gnupg \
lsb-release -y

sudo mkdir -p /etc/apt/keyrings
curl -fsSL https://download.docker.com/linux/ubuntu/gpg | sudo gpg --dearmor -o /etc/apt/keyrings/docker.gpg
echo \
"deb [arch=$(dpkg --print-architecture) signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/docker.gpg] \
https://download.docker.com/linux/ubuntu \
$(lsb_release -cs) stable" | \
sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/docker.list > /dev/null

sudo apt update
sudo apt install docker-ce docker-ce-cli containerd.io docker-buildx-plugin docker-compose-plugin -y

sudo systemctl enable docker
sudo systemctl start docker

newgrp docker

docker --version
docker run hello-world
  1. Clone the Repository: Clone the repository by going inside your target directory and running the following commands in terminal:
git clone <repository-url>
cd AI_Studio_CoE
  1. Set Up a Virtual Environment: Run the following commands in the same terminal: 
python3.10 -m venv .doc_env
source .doc_env/bin/activate
  1. Install Dependencies: Run the following commands in the same terminal to install the required packages:
pip install -r req.txt
  1. Install YOLOv10: Run the following commands in the same terminal to download and install YOLOv10:
git clone https://github.com/THU-MIG/yolov10.git
cd yolov10
pip install .
cd ..
  1. Set OpenAI API Key for LLM Evaluation 
    export OPENAI_API_KEY="your-openai-gpt-3.5-t-api-key"

docs.title: Getting Started with pipeline
docs.text: A typical document AI appplication consists of certain elements in its pipeline. These elements are as follows:

docs.title: 1. Pre-Processing:
docs.text: Pre-processing is done to obtain the information of file type, language and reducing the anomalies using image processing.

docs.title: 2. Identification:
docs.text: Then the layout and structure detection of processed file is carried out in identification.

docs.title: 3. Extraction:
docs.text: After detecting the layout and structure, information extraction is done only from the selected elements of the layout.

docs.title: 4. Post processing:
docs.text: The information extracted is either used in more complex downstream extraction or displayed to the user.

docs.title: 5. Observability:
docs.text: After the application is made, observability is used to keep an eye on the system resources and api calls.

docs.title: 6. Storage:
docs.text: The vectorization/indexing of the document is needed in many extraction tasks. These indexes are saved in databases for future queries.

Core Functionalities
docs.text: Infinity Extraction provides a comprehensive set of features for document processing, data extraction, evaluation, and observability, leveraging advanced models like YOLOv10, Microsoft's Table Transformer (TATR), and PaddleNLP.

docs.title: Preprocess
docs.text: The preprocessing module prepares documents and images for analysis with tools for text extraction, PDF conversion, and image enhancement.

docs.title: Text & Bounding Box Extractor
docs.text:
• Extracts text and precise bounding box coordinates from PDFs using pdfminer.six.
  • Transforms coordinates to a top-left origin system for consistency.
  • Outputs a dictionary with text and bounding box data for structured processing.

docs.title: Create Searchable PDF
docs.text:
• Converts scanned or non-searchable PDFs into searchable PDFs using OCR.
  • Preserves original layout while enabling text selection.
  • Includes utilities to:
  • Extract images from PDFs as a list of tuples (List[(PIL_Image, page_number)]).
  • Verify if a PDF is searchable, returning a boolean.

docs.title: Image Preprocessing
docs.text:
• Offers a suite of operations to enhance document images:
  • Resolution Enhancement: Increases DPI (enhance_dpi).
  • Image Enhancement: Increases sharpness and contrast (enhance_image).
  • Derasterization: Removes watermarks, gridlines and stamps (derasterize).
  • Thresholding: Removes shadows and lighting inconsistencies (adaptive_threshold, threshold_advanced).
  • Noise Removal: Eliminates artifacts (noise_removal,denoise_advanced).
  • Deskewing: Corrects image skew (deskew).
  • Contrast Enhancement: Improves readability (enhance_contrast).
  • Image Resizing: Adjusts dimensions (resize_image).
  • Edge Detection: Identifies structural edges (edge_detection).
  • Border Removal: Removes unwanted borders (remove_border).
  • Thinning & Skeletonization: Simplifies image structure (thinning, skeletonization).
  • Rotation: Corrects orientation (rotate).
  • Supports PIL Images, NumPy arrays, or image paths, returning processed PIL Images.

docs.title: Document Layout Detection & Table Extraction
docs.text:
• Detects document layouts (e.g., tables, headers) in PDFs or images using YOLOv10.
  • Extracts bounding boxes and exports tables to Excel files.
  • Provides annotated images, structured layout data, and cropped images for specified elements (e.g., tables).

docs.title: Extraction
docs.text: The extraction module focuses on extracting structured and unstructured data from documents.

docs.title: Table Detection
docs.text:
• Identifies table regions, including rotated tables, using Microsoft's Table Transformer (TATR).
  • Returns cropped table images and metadata (confidence scores, bounding boxes).
  • Configurable with class thresholds and crop padding.

docs.title: Table Structure Recognition (TSR)
docs.text:
• Extracts table structures from images using TATR and saves them as CSV files.
  • Supports visualization of table structures and customizable image resizing.

docs.title: Document Visual Question Answering (VQA)
docs.text: Useful in extractin data from pages having content in key value pairs. - Answers natural language questions about document content using PaddleNLP's Document Intelligence Taskflow. - Supports single-document queries, batch processing, and direct chat-style QA.

docs.title: Document QA Service
docs.text:
• Integrates with database to track extraction progress and manage active sessions.
  • Retrieves model training questions for ongoing sessions.

docs.title: Structured Chunking
docs.text: Useful in structured content extraction from documents containing paragraphs and tables. - Extracts tables and filters them using filtering_table_pipeline. - Processes headers with main_pipeline_create_put_table_headers and organizes content hierarchically. - Merges multi-page tables and maps them to headers. - Extracts table of contents (TOC) data with customised_toc_extraction_pipeline.

docs.title: LLM Evaluation
docs.text: Evaluates Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines and LLM outputs for accuracy and reliability.

docs.title: RAG Pipeline Evaluation
docs.text:
• Measures performance with metrics like:
  • Faithfulness: Alignment with provided context.
  • Relevancy: Relevance to the query.
  • Precision and Recall: Accuracy with or without ground truth.
  • Uses RAGAS and DeepEval frameworks.

docs.title: Risk Assessment
docs.text:
• Detects issues in LLM outputs:
  • Hallucination: Fabricated or unsupported information.
  • Bias: Biased content detection.
  • Toxicity: Harmful or inappropriate language.

docs.title: Summarization Evaluation
docs.text:
• Assesses summary quality using:
  • Semantic Similarity: BERTScore for contextual accuracy.
  • N-gram Metrics: BLEU and ROUGE for word-level evaluation.

docs.title: Post-Process
docs.text: Provides tools for extracted data to be either displayed to user or use it in some downstream task

docs.title: Citation
docs.text:
Use for highlighting and displaying the field the extractor has extracted.

  • Extracts text from searchable and scanned PDFs using PyMuPDF and OCR engines (Tesseract, PaddleOCR, EasyOCR).
  • Matches fields and values with fuzzywuzzy for robust handling of text variations.
  • Returns JSON with citations, including bounding boxes, confidence scores, and matched text.

A sample application which does a basic multi page vqa and shows the result via citaion is provided in repository as 'citation_engine_app.py'. Citation shows the results on UI so to see this application in action a UI is needed. To run the application backend, run the following command: 

uvicorn citation_engine_app:app --reload --host 0.0.0.0 --port < port_number >

docs.title: To see the citation_engine_app working, click on this video link
Semantic Matching
docs.text:
Use for extracting the sentences semantically similar to the reference sentence from the user.

  • Matches predefined query sentences against PDF text passages using semantic similarity with the all-mpnet-base-v2 sentence transformer model.
  • Returns a dictionary with key as reference sentence and value as the matched sentences.

docs.title: Observability
docs.text:
Provides OpenTelemetry-based observability for FastAPI or Flask applications:

  • Tracing: Instruments endpoints with OpenTelemetry Tracer and supports custom spans via @traced.
  • Metrics: Exports service metrics to external backends.
  • Logging: Logs to console and file (/var/log/app.log) with customizable formats.

docs.title: If GPU is present then:
docs.text:
Run the following bash command to go in side observability and up the docker image. 

# bash
cd wissenai/observability/docker-config-gpu
sudo docker compose up -d

docs.title: If GPU is not present then:
docs.text:
Run the following bash command to go in side observability and up the docker image. 

# bash
cd wissenai/observability/docker-config-no-gpu
sudo docker compose up -d
Powered by Grafana, accessible at localhost:3000 after Docker setup. - Displays tracing, metrics, and logging data for application monitoring.

  • Skip at the login screen.

A sample fast_app.py and flask_app.py for tracing and logging is in the repository. To run the app for testing the dashboard run the following command: 

# bash

## For fast_app.py
python fast_app.py

## For flask_app.py
python flask_app.py

Demo Pipeline
docs.text:
We will be creating a pipeline which takes a noisy pdf as an input, converts it into image, do some image processing to make it readable and then perform a VQA on the resulting image.

For this demo a 1 page invoice was selected 

# python
## Converting the pdf to image
from wissenai.preprocess.searchable_pdf import *

images = extract_images_from_pdf('/path/to/pdf')
images is a list of tuples in the form of List[(PIL_Image, page_number)]

The image of first page is images[0][0]

# python
## To resolve the rotation present in the image
from wissenai.preprocess.utils import de_skew

deskewed = de_skew(image = images[0][0])
deskewed is an opencv image.

Now we see that the image coming out of pdf is unresonably large in size. It is rendered with 600 dpi which might be too much for the image processing.

# python
## To resize the deskewed to a reasonable size

resized = cv2.resize(deskewed, (deskewed.shape[0]//10,deskewed.shape[1]//10))
resized is a much resonably sized image

Now there are some shadows/non-uniform lighting in image which can cause problem in VQA.

# python
## To resolve shadows/non-uniform lighting we will use adaptive thresholding
from wissenai.preprocess.utils import adaptive_threshold

thresh_image = adaptive_threshold(image = resized)
thresh_image is an opencv image.

Thresholding removes the shadows but introduces some artifacts and noise. We will try to denoise it.

# python
## To resolve the noise we will use noise_removal function
from wissenai.preprocess.utils import noise_removal

denoised = noise_removal(image = thresh_image)
denoised is PIL image

# python
## Saving the final image

denoised.save("denoised.jpg")
Now we will do the VQA

# python
## For VQA we will use the docvqa chat function
from wissenai.vqa.docvqa import chat

answer = chat(_path = "denoised.jpg", question = "What is the Invoice Number?")
answer will be a string

This pipeline leverages preprocessing, image processing, and VQA features to deliver accurate results from noisy inputs.

docs.title: Models Used
docs.text:
• YOLOv10: For layout detection and table extraction.
  • Microsoft Table Transformer (TATR): For table detection and structure recognition.
  • PaddleNLP: For document VQA.
  • RAGAS, DeepEval, BERTScore, BLEU, ROUGE: For LLM evaluation.

from wissenai.preprocess.utils import *

import ipywidgets as widgets
from IPython.display import display, clear_output
from PIL import Image
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Define your MCQ-style choices using RadioButtons
mcq_widget = widgets.RadioButtons(
    options=['adaptive', 'otsu'],
    description='method',
    disabled=False
)

# Define a slider (int in this case)
block_widget = widgets.IntSlider(
    value=15,
    min=3,
    max=30,
    step=2,
    description='block_size',
    continuous_update=True
)

c_widget = widgets.IntSlider(
    value=10,
    min=0,
    max=20,
    step=1,
    description='C',
    continuous_update=True
)

output = widgets.Output()

# --- Callback ---
def update_image(change=None):
    method = mcq_widget.value
    block_size = block_widget.value
    C = c_widget.value

    try:
        # Call your threshold function
        processed = threshold_advanced(
            image=deskewed,
            method=method,
            block_size=block_size,
            C=C
        )

        with output:
            clear_output(wait=True)
            plt.figure(figsize=(20, 20))
            plt.imshow(processed, cmap='gray')
            plt.axis('off')
            plt.title(f"Method: {method}, Block: {block_size}, C: {C}")
            plt.show()

    except Exception as e:
        with output:
            clear_output(wait=True)
            print(f"Error: {e}")

# Attach events
mcq_widget.observe(update_image, names='value')
block_widget.observe(update_image, names='value')
c_widget.observe(update_image, names='value')

# Display
display(widgets.VBox([mcq_widget, block_widget, c_widget, output]))

# Initial render
update_image()
